text:
Ana V: Heads-up — started seeing p99 tail spikes when requests hit the CUTLASS fallback for seq <= 32 with KV cache warm. Looks like ‘smearing’ across batches, not a single noisy request. Anyone on this?

Ryan L: I noticed that too after the router tweak last night. Dashboard shows p50 steady but p99 up ~3x around 02:10 UTC. I pulled a short perf profile.

perf-bot: alert: route=gen-1 / p99 latency crossed 180ms (baseline 60ms) at 2026-03-15T02:10:12Z :eyes:

Ryan L: Profile snippet (hot path kernel times, seq=32, kv_hit=true):
```
kernel         time_ms  calls  avg_ms   notes
triton_exec     8.1     120    0.067   small-batch opt
cutlass_exec   42.3     28     1.51    high variance, syncs
kv_lookup       0.6     148    0.004
batch_pack      1.2     20     0.06
-- thread stats: cutlass path shows wakeups and tail spikes for coalesced batches
```

Ryan L: Key observation: when KV is hot we get more tight-affinity requests (same key set). Those requests get routed to a node running CUTLASS fallback more often because router thinks the smaller batch size + lower mem pressure favors CUTLASS, but CUTLASS path ends up doing syncs that cause cross-batch blocking.

Sasha P: That matches my microbench. CUTLASS has worse overlap with async KV prefetch for these short seqs. When multiple requests with same KV keys land, CUTLASS kernels serialize on a CUDA stream we didn't expect.

Mike J: Repro command I used locally: `rbench --model=redwood/gpt-small --seq=32 --kv-warm --concurrency=16 --routes=force-cutlass`
Output snippet: `p99=340ms p95=120ms p50=45ms`. Swap to `--routes=force-triton` -> `p99=95ms p95=70ms p50=42ms`.

Ana V: So it's not purely kernel perf — it's an interaction: KV affinity -> small, coalesced batches -> CUTLASS chosen -> stream syncs -> batch-smearing across requests. We need a fix in the router/autotune.

Ryan L: Proposed quick mitigations:
- add kv_affinity_bias to the routing score so requests with kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.5 prefer Triton
- increase cutlass_probe_cooldown_ms to avoid flip-flopping when we see a burst of KV-hot traffic

Sasha P: Also we should track `kv_affinity_group_id` in telemetry so we can see when many requests share the same hot keys. Right now we only have kv_hit_rate which hides group collisions.

Mike J: Suggested config patch (quick experiment):
```
"router_autotune": {
  "cutlass_probe_threshold": 0.15,
  "cutlass_probe_cooldown_ms": 5000,
  "kv_affinity_bias": 0.7,
  "score_formula": "latency_weight*pred + cost_weight*pred*(1-kv_affinity_bias)")
}
```
Note: that's a sketch not direct JSON we ship.

Ryan L: If we add kv_affinity_bias, we should also make it per-model and let dedicated pools override. Otherwise large-traffic models will always be forced to Triton and we lose cutlass wins elsewhere.

Sasha P: For longer-term: autotuner should include a feature for `kv_group_collision_rate` and prefer kernels that allow better async overlap with KV prefetch. We can expose a small perf counter from runtime: `cuda_stream_sync_waits` per kernel.

Ana V: OK. Short plan: (1) add a conservative router rule: when kv_hit_rate > 0.6 AND seq <= 48 -> prefer triton, (2) bump cutlass probe cooldown to 5s, (3) add telemetry for kv_affinity_group_id. Can we ship (1)+(2) as a canary today?

Ryan L: I'll patch router config and run a 10% canary on gen-1 routes. Will also add a debug flag to log kv_affinity_group_id for traces in that canary.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: config=router-v2-kv-affinity-20260315 canary=10% target=gen-1

perf-bot: note: perf regression guard on gen-1 disabled for canary (manual review)

Mike J: I ran a quick canary sim in staging with kv-hot traffic and saw p99 drop from ~320ms -> ~110ms on the canary nodes. Promising.

Ana V: Great. Please paste the router change PR and add a short runbook entry explaining why KV-hot should bias toward Triton. We should also add a follow-up issue to make autotune learn `kv_group_collision_rate`.

Ryan L: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/routers/pulls/1289 (contains test matrices and staging results). I'll open the follow-up issue.

Sasha P: I'll add the `cuda_stream_sync_waits` counter to the runtime telemetry next sprint.

Ana V: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open until we confirm the canary at 24h. :thumbsup:
